fields.value: Support Vast.ai GPU rentals alongside RunPod

Jack Heart requests an Auto task in the Etude SDK repository to support [Vast.ai](<http://Vast.ai>) in addition to RunPod (2026-11-04 UTC). Add a usable second GPU rental provider through the existing Etude launcher, retaining RunPod support. Proceed through the Auto graph, publish and ship after its checks.

Problem and beneficiary
Manabot MTG-213 needs bounded GPU training. Recent configured RunPod A6000/L4/A4000/A4500 offers were unavailable at the required shapes and price ceilings. Another provider lets callers use available capacity without rewriting experiments or operating rentals manually. This does not establish that [Vast.ai](<http://Vast.ai>) currently has suitable capacity. The SDK lives in loopflowstudio/etude, /Users/jack/src/etude; etude-studio is a separate service repository.

Outcome and acceptance

* Configure [Vast.ai](<http://Vast.ai>) credentials and rental requirements through Etude's public Python/API and thin CLI conventions. Show a documented end-to-end example alongside RunPod.
* Search/filter actual offers, expose availability and an honest bounded quote, rent a compatible GPU instance, bootstrap the existing worker, execute an ordinary Run/cohort and retain outputs through the existing evidence path.
* Integrate with existing Machine/Allocation/Rental ownership rather than adding another scheduler or training runner. Preserve source/run identity, provider/hardware provenance, timeout semantics and caller-selected provider behavior.
* Account for provider-specific compute, storage and other applicable charges when bounding cost. Do not label an incomplete quote a guaranteed total. Preserve allocation/cohort caps and rental deadlines; paid creation remains an explicit action.
* Recover uncertain creation replies without duplicate paid instances; reconcile owned inventory/status/billing; terminate only owned rentals. Demonstrate cleanup across normal completion, bootstrap failure, caller loss, cancellation and deadline expiry. The deadline guardian must work before installing client dependencies, as for RunPod.
* Preserve RunPod behavior, owned SSH machines and credential-free local reads. Do not introduce automatic cross-provider retries that can duplicate work or exceed a shared budget. Provider selection may be explicit for this first addition.
* Add controlled, network-mocked lifecycle/failure and resource-counting tests plus normal repository checks. Never intentionally induce host load. Record evidence limits honestly if live [Vast.ai](<http://Vast.ai>) validation lacks credentials or a separately authorized spend allowance.

Boundaries and context
MTG-213 retains its own $10 cumulative training budget, frozen 134-deck population, prepared run and live Graph. This Task does not inherit that budget, allocate a pilot GPU, alter its protocol or relaunch its work. No new paid test allowance is supplied here. Implementation and deterministic validation can proceed without buying capacity. Credentials must remain injected and never appear in output or artifacts. RunPod credentials for existing campaigns are in Doppler etude/prd; [Vast.ai](<http://Vast.ai>) credentials have not been verified.

Research starting points (verify current official behavior): [https://vast.ai/developers/api](<https://vast.ai/developers/api>) and [https://cloud.vast.ai/cli/](<https://cloud.vast.ai/cli/>) cover offer search, SSH instance creation, instance management and destruction. Existing integration points include src/etude/launch/machines.py (Machines protocol), src/etude/launch/providers/runpod/, providers/package.py and [cleanup.py](<http://cleanup.py>). Keep the design small and domain-typed; do not commit to a speculative provider abstraction before reading the current implementation.

Overlap checked at filing
No open PR directly changes the provider modules. Nearby open work: #59 (branch jack/mtg175-output-delivery, MTG-175) changes worker/courier.py and output-delivery tests; #56 (jack/mtg175-eval-queue, MTG-175) changes evaluation queuing and [cli.py/experiment.py](<http://cli.py/experiment.py>); #58 (jack/mtg175-report-metrics, MTG-175) changes reports/tracking. Preserve those owners' changes and decisions if integration reaches these paths. EXP-14 is an unstarted owned-pool/on-demand vocabulary task; EXP-12 is an unstarted database-migration task. Neither is permission to take over their scope. Reconcile actual main and overlap before editing.
